pattern.top_pattern: VERACYTE lab spend is obscured by Not Mapped classification
pattern.what_is_impacting: NC / IA / MO / TN / WA Medicaid / OP Lab/Pthlgy and Not Mapped facility classification
pattern.pattern_details: VERACYTE spend is appearing under Not Mapped facility or service classification across multiple states, with the clearest clinical concentration in NC outpatient lab and pathology. Because the same provider also appears in operational Not Mapped buckets, this is a gating data-quality and routing issue before drawing strong conclusions about utilization or reimbursement. The current classification can hide the real site of care, benefit rules, and authorization pathway.
pattern.why_it_matters: If mapping is wrong, the business can misfire on UM, provider, and pricing actions because the claims are not being interpreted in the right service category.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Correct the facility and service mapping for VERACYTE claims, then re-run authorization, edit, and reimbursement review on the cleaned category before taking provider or utilization action.
pattern.validation_reason: The pattern repeatedly involves Not Mapped values and unmapped classification, so data validation is required before using it as a true provider performance signal.
evidence_summary: NC outpatient lab and pathology tied to VERACYTE added about +$58K, mostly from diagnoses E042 and E041.
Operational Not Mapped VERACYTE spend added about +$42K across NC, MO, and IA.
A separate utilization-only Not Mapped signal added about +$17K across WA and TN.
All contributing groups carry Not Mapped or unmapped flags.
